description:
## Goal

No `.fz` source may look covered while its owning test discards the compiler
outcome, swallows a panic, or never reaches the user-facing door appropriate to
its purpose.

Give every source in `fixtures2/` a machine-checkable contract:

- behavioural programs are scored through their declared `fz2` paths;
- parser/compiler-shape fixtures are checked by a phase-specific assertion;
- known-red outcomes surface as explicit ignored trials with an owning ticket;
- no fixture is admitted merely because its basename appears in a test or a
  corpus loop returned.

Do not blindly run every numbered source through all three doors. The repository
intentionally separates behavioural fixtures from parser/compiler fixtures, and
many numbered sources are negative, partial, or shape-primary cases.

## Verified current state

Verified on clean `origin/main`
`a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`.

The corpus contains 597 `.fz` files:

- 163 under `fixtures2/behavior/`;
- 434 directly under `fixtures2/`.

`tests/fixture_matrix.rs::discover()` reads only `fixtures2/behavior/`. Its
current inventory is 485 dynamic path trials plus 9 static trials. Nine dynamic
trials are ignored: every path of `enumerable_protocol_dispatch`, `enum_tier0`,
and `fz_f98_map_reduce`.

That boundary is documented and historical, not an accidental recursive-walk
bug. `.agent/docs/fixtures.md` and `fixtures2/GOLDEN.md` define behavioural
fixtures as the `fixtures2/behavior/` population and define numbered root files
as compiler/parser media unless they explicitly opt into another contract.
Commits `c94614d59`, `8a26e140f`, and `b59d96d6e` introduced that split and its
routing.

The original ticket's supporting claims are therefore stale:

- matrix file coverage is 163/597 = 27.3%, not 140/574 = 24%;
- there are no root-level `*.expected.txt` or `*.expected.diagnostics`
  sidecars; the only numbered sidecars are six compiler-contract
  `*.call_edges` snapshots;
- root fixtures are not all ungated: 425 basenames occur in Rust tests, six
  compiler contracts are discovered dynamically, and 340 exact-`fn main()`
  roots enter the return-widening corpus shards.

The real defect is that much of that ownership is non-asserting.

`fixtures2/00424_protocol_no_impl.fz` is the concrete witness:

- `cargo test --test fixture_matrix 00424_protocol_no_impl` runs zero trials;
- `fz2 interp`, `fz2 run`, and `fz2 build` each exit 101 by panicking at
  `jobs/artifact.rs:155`:
  `product materialization should have complete call edges after waits`;
- `port_planner_test::protocol_call_on_non_implementing_type_emits_diagnostic`
  nevertheless passes because it executes `let _ = compiler.drive();` and
  contains only a TODO about the diagnostic it claims to test;
- the fixture is also in return-widening shard 0, which passes because that
  sweep discards the drive result and asserts only that widening did not occur.

There are currently 32 `let _ = compiler.drive()` sites and four
`catch_unwind(... compiler.drive())` sites in compiler tests. These are the
first population to classify: some have legitimate phase-local assertions
elsewhere, while others are vacuous green coverage or hidden known-red cases.

Three numbered sources have neither a basename owner nor compiler-contract
metadata:

- `00011_cond_specialization.fz`;
- `00012_projection_boundary_abi.fz`;
- `00028_helper_roots.fz`.

The first two happen to enter the widening sweep; `00028` does not because its
entry is spelled `fn main(), ...`.

## Strategy

### 1. Make ownership explicit

Introduce one authoritative fixture-ownership inventory derived from source
metadata or an equally reviewable checked registry. It must enumerate every
`.fz` recursively and classify it as one or more real contract media:

- behavioural matrix;
- compiler contract;
- parser success/diagnostic;
- focused compiler phase assertion;
- explicit known-red deferral with an owning ticket.

Multiple media are allowed when the source genuinely proves independent facts,
but every declared owner must name an observable assertion. A textual
`include_str!`, discarded result, TODO, manual sweep recipe, or caught panic is
not ownership.

Add a test that fails when a fixture is unclassified, names a missing owner, or
names a known-red exclusion without a rationale and ticket.

### 2. Use the existing matrix participation model

`FixtureMetadata::participates_in_matrix()` already distinguishes behavioural
policy from compiler-contract policy. Refactor matrix discovery so that it
finds:

- every `.fz` under `fixtures2/behavior/`, preserving today's default routing;
- any source elsewhere under `fixtures2/` whose metadata explicitly
  participates in the matrix.

A compiler-contract-only root file must not accidentally default onto all three
behavioural paths. Add focused discovery tests for:

- a root matrix participant;
- a root compiler-contract-only source;
- an ordinary root source with no matrix metadata;
- a behavioral-directory source using default routes;
- an explicitly deferred root path.

Each selected `(fixture, path)` must remain an individually named
`libtest-mimic` trial.

### 3. Replace vacuous green tests with contracts

Audit the 32 discarded `compiler.drive()` results and four swallowed panics.

For each site:

- assert the intended successful phase/product and its observable result;
- assert the intended diagnostic code and relevant payload;
- or convert a genuinely known-red case into an explicit ignored contract with
  an owning ticket and stable reason.

Do not preserve “pre-existing pipeline gap” comments as passing tests. Do not
make a blanket known-red list that says only that a file is excluded.

Start RED with `00424_protocol_no_impl`:

- it must be visible in the ownership inventory;
- it must be visible as a matrix trial rather than producing zero filtered
  tests;
- until `fz-kdt.77` lands, its three paths may be explicitly deferred to that
  ticket;
- when `fz-kdt.77` lands, remove those deferrals and require a non-panicking
  `expect: diagnostic` contract on `interp`, `run`, and `build`.

Classify and assert `00011`, `00012`, and `00028` rather than relying on their
incidental widening-sweep eligibility.

### 4. Preserve phase-specific and manual sweep intent

Keep parser-negative sources in parser tests with exact expected diagnostics.
Keep compiler-shape sources in the compiler-contract harness. Keep stress and
canonical-output sweeps as additional evidence, not as substitutes for an
expected outcome: parity between two identical panics is not correctness.

The return-widening corpus shards may remain, but document that they prove only
termination/no widening and do not own compilation success, diagnostics, or
runtime behavior.

### 5. Documentation and obsolete text

Update `.agent/docs/fixtures.md`, `fixtures2/GOLDEN.md`, and the matrix module
documentation with the explicit ownership/discovery rules and the distinction
between phase-local, behavioural, and known-red contracts.

Repair README's stale links to nonexistent `fixtures/index.md` and
`fixtures/GOLDEN.md`; point it to the actual fixture documentation and
`fixtures2/GOLDEN.md`.

Delete TODO-only “tests,” obsolete “pre-existing gap” comments, and any
temporary census code once every fixture has an asserted owner.

## Acceptance

- A checked inventory accounts for all 597 current `.fz` sources and fails on a
  newly added unclassified source.
- No inventory entry treats a discarded result, caught panic, basename mention,
  or manual comparison sweep as a passing contract.
- Matrix discovery still includes all 163 behavioural-directory sources and
  additionally includes explicit root-level matrix participants.
- Compiler-contract-only root fixtures remain out of the behavioural matrix.
- `00424_protocol_no_impl` is no longer invisible: it is either an explicit
  ignored trial owned by `fz-kdt.77`, or, after that fix, a green three-path
  diagnostic fixture. It must never again yield zero matrix trials.
- Every current `let _ = compiler.drive()` and caught-drive panic is replaced by
  an asserted outcome or an explicit ticketed deferral.
- `00011`, `00012`, and `00028` have declared, asserted owners.
- Existing compiler contracts and parser surface tests remain green.
- Record before/after matrix trial counts, active/ignored counts, and
  single-threaded wall time. CI retains `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1`; do not add an
  independent conflicting thread-control convention.
- Run the focused discovery/ownership regressions, compiler-contract tests,
  parser fixture tests, `cargo test --test fixture_matrix -- --test-threads=1`,
  the full workspace suite, formatting, and clippy with warnings denied.
title: Require explicit, asserted gate ownership for every fixtures2 source
